newsitem.title: USA: BP announces Liberty oil discovery.
newsitem.headline: BP announces Liberty oil discovery.

text.p: British Petroleum Co Plc's Alaska unit said on Thursday it had struck oil at its offshore Liberty prospect on the North Slope.
BP Exploration (Alaska) Inc said the Liberty discovery holds about 120 million recoverable barrels, an amount the company believes will be commercially worthwhile to develop.

Liberty is about five miles offshore in the Beaufort Sea, about 11 miles southeast of the Endicott development. It is about five miles from the site of the pipeline planned to connect BP's Badami field, now in development, to oil field infrastructure, BP Alaska spokesman Paul Laird said.
In the past, oil companies have been reluctant to develop small offshore North Slope fields outside the state's three-mile territorial limit.
But oil companies have learned to make such developments more cost-effective, Laird said.

"We figure that the cost cutting and the technology advances in the last few years have made us confident that we can make developments in the 100 (million) to 150 million barrels range commercial," he said.
The company said it plans further evaluation of drilling and seismic studies to better determine the extent of the discovery.
BP plans to develop the site, located in water about 20 feet (six metres) deep, from a new gravel island it hopes to construct, Laird said.
BP acquired acreage for the Liberty prospect in a federal lease sale held last September. The company bid about $10 million for three tracts in the area, Laird said.
Oil was first discovered in the area in 1982 by Shell, but that company later relinquished its leases to the federal government.
Although several companies have discovered oil in the federally owned outer continental shelf on Alaska's North Slope, prohibitive costs have previously precluded commercial production.
